label: Index cards
thesis: Keep to the site's paper look: a plain sign-up card, a ruled preferences card with four labelled rows (areas, near, towns, venues) shown as pills, and a text-first email grouped by day.
risk: Four separate rows with pills can feel like a settings form, and it gives no clue how many shows a choice brings in until it's saved.

label: Sentence builder
thesis: Choices read as one sentence ('Email me shows in Greater Boston, within 25 miles of 02139...') so the any-of-these rule is obvious and sign-up is a single short page.
risk: Sentence slots are a less familiar control, are harder to make accessible and to use on a phone, and the 20-choice limit may make the sentence long.

label: Live preview
thesis: A preferences page with checkbox lists on the left and a preview of next week's email on the right, with match counts beside each choice, so people see what they'll get.
risk: Needs counts and a preview computed per request, and the two-pane layout must collapse to one column on phones.
